soundness_flags.label: lem:cdf-score-martingale
soundness_flags.one_line: The stated predictable quadratic variation is algebraically false: the HT increment at Q_a,N(q) has diagonal factor 1{Y_i(a)<=Q_a,N(q)}^2/f_a(q)^2, whereas the proposed loss uses (q-1{Y_i(a)<=Q_a,N(q)})^2/f_a(q)^2; their cross terms likewise differ.

soundness_flags.label: def:finite-population-class and thm:anytime-qte-coverage
soundness_flags.one_line: The finite-population local-linearity condition makes M empty: for any finite step CDF and continuum q, F_a,N(Q_a,N(q))-q is generically nonzero, so the displayed ratio diverges as h tends to zero; moreover tau_t is used throughout although only tau_N is defined and the estimator at t targets a prefix rather than an unobserved terminal population.

soundness_flags.label: prop:homogeneous-special-case
soundness_flags.one_line: Its subclass is empty: u_i,1,N(q)^2=u_i,0,N(q)^2 together with u_i,1,N(q)u_i,0,N(q)=0 forces both scores to be zero, impossible for q in (0,1), and inconsistent with score nondegeneracy.

soundness_flags.label: prop:regret-width-identity
soundness_flags.one_line: “Locally LIL exact” is neither defined nor supplied by a statement or assumption; anytime coverage plus the proposed lower bound does not establish the equality that the frontier question uses.

soundness_flags.label: ass:uniform-local-quantile-linearity and ass:uniform-score-kernel
soundness_flags.one_line: These are tagged as standard ZhangZheng2020 finite-population variants, but that paper studies stochastic covariate-adaptive randomization and fixed-horizon QTE asymptotics, not the displayed discrete-array local derivative condition or a limiting fixed-array score kernel; retag and justify a feasible replacement.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Econometrics 249, Part A (2025), article 105857
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article proposes fully adaptive and multistage covariate-adjusted response-adaptive designs for QTE estimation, establishes asymptotic efficiency, and studies fixed-sample asymptotic inference; it does not present an anytime whole-curve finite-population frontier.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2502.17427; cited ICML proceedings version was not publicly inspectable through the proceedings endpoint
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The preprint studies design-based ATE estimation, gives an anytime logarithmic-order Neyman-regret design under boundedness assumptions, and discusses scalar adaptive-IPW confidence intervals.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1704 abstract; pp. 1705–1706 equations (1)–(2); p. 1713 Theorem 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives i.i.d. quantile confidence sequences uniform over time and all quantiles, with a finite empirical-process LIL inequality and square-root log-log rate.

The paper gives time- and value-uniform CDF bounds for running averaged conditional distributions, including an importance-weighted counterfactual-distribution extension, while noting that bounds can be trivial on hard instances.

The published article derives uniform-on-a-compact-quantile-set asymptotic distributions and bootstrap inference for simple and IPW QTE estimators under covariate-adaptive randomization; it does not state the proposal's finite-population step-CDF local-linearity or score-kernel assumptions.
The paper develops efficient A2IPW inference and confidence sequences for scalar ATEs in adaptive experiments, not quantile-process inference.
The paper formulates a minimax multi-objective Pareto trade-off between welfare regret and statistical power for ATE inference and constructs Pareto-optimal bandit designs.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Re-derive the randomization influence process from the actual HT CDF increment, then redefine the loss, regret, benchmark, and frontier from its true predictable quadratic variation; alternatively specify a different centered-score estimator whose martingale increment genuinely has the proposed score.

Choose one coherent asymptotic experiment: either define nested prefix-population targets tau_t with a feasible lattice-scale finite-population quantile condition, or move to a continuous superpopulation model; then rewrite coverage and band honesty for that target.

Replace the impossible homogeneous condition by aggregate symmetry conditions that actually imply p-star=1/2, and add a separately stated LIL-exactness theorem or an explicit conditional scope for the regret-width identity.

recommended_next_step: Reject the current kernel and redraft from a correct HT quantile-score martingale and nonempty asymptotic class before re-running novelty review.
